"
On August 23, an Indian tourist named Vijaya Lakshmi Gali experienced a tragic incident in Kuala Lumpur when the pavement suddenly gave way beneath her feet. She fell into an 8-meter-deep sinkhole and vanished from sight. Rescuers have been searching for her since the incident occurred, but have only discovered her slippers as evidence of her presence.

***

The search and rescue operation has employed various sophisticated methods to locate the missing woman. Ground-penetrating radar, remote cameras, and tracker units have been used in the extensive effort to find her. Despite these technological resources, no significant trace of her has been found in the underground location.

***

* By the eighth day of the search operation, authorities determined that continuing the rescue efforts posed too great a risk to the personnel involved in the recovery attempt.

***

The decision to halt the search was made by Malaysia's fire and rescue department, with Dr Zaliha Mustafa emphasizing that the safety of the rescue personnel was a paramount concern. Two divers who entered early on Thursday had to be withdrawn because conditions were deemed too hazardous for human entry. Additionally, authorities had flushed portions of the underground drainage framework using high-pressure water jets and excavators to clear debris from the area.

***

Officials noted that a similar soil collapse had been reported at the same location during the previous year, suggesting that the ground in this area may be structurally unstable. This history of geological instability adds another layer of concern regarding the safety risks of continuing the rescue mission in such treacherous underground conditions.

Is there anything else I can help with?
"
